title: Ticket Orders Carried on One Household Account
content:
A household account may carry several Lift Tickets orders at once, up to 10, counting orders that stand as ordered, paid, issued or in use. Orders that have reached used up, expired, cancelled, refunded or closed no longer count against the account.

One order covers one product for one holder. A party skiing on different products holds one order each, so four skiers on two different products of the line are carried as four orders rather than as one.

A product sold with a named holder is never opened twice for the same holder over the same named ski date; the second order is treated as a duplicate of the first, and the household is asked whether they meant a different holder or a different date.

## The basis on which the duplicate is judged

The duplicate test rests on the collective's own order records rather than on what the household recalls, and it is made before the second order is opened. The records are matched on three things together: the household account, the named holder and the named ski date. Only orders standing as ordered, paid, issued or in use are looked at; an order that has reached any of the settled states is not a duplicate of anything. Two records that differ in the product or in the mountain are separate orders rather than one order and its duplicate.

## How the two counts read together

| Two Lift Tickets orders on one household account | Both count against the 10 | The second is a duplicate of the first |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Same named holder, same named ski date, same product and mountain, both standing paid | yes | yes |
| Same named holder, same named ski date, different products | yes | no |
| Same named holder, different named ski dates | yes | no |
| An earlier order standing refunded and a later one standing ordered, same holder and date | only the later one | no |

The rows above are hypothetical pairs offered to read the two rules against one another: the count of orders on the account turns on the state the order stands in, while the duplicate test turns on the household account, the holder and the ski date together, among orders that are not yet settled.
